units.function: HTTP integration test requiring fixed authentication, cookie, CSRF and API-key header paths to be redacted by Pino and proving request/response cookie and authorization values do not appear in serialized output.
units.dependencyDirection: Node HTTP request/response headers enter pino-http; a shared list of Pino redact paths is applied before the serialized log reaches a writable sink.
units.keyDataModels: Request/response headers, authorization/cookie/set-cookie/proxy-authorization/CSRF/XSRF/API-key names, Pino redaction paths and [Redacted] marker.
units.lifecycle: A real ephemeral HTTP server receives credential-bearing headers and emits one JSON log; the test verifies selected request/response values are absent and four header locations contain the redaction marker.
units.testAssessment: The real logger/server path is stronger than testing a constant alone and covers request plus response secrets. Only authorization, cookie and set-cookie are exercised end to end; proxy authorization, CSRF/XSRF and API key are list-membership assertions. Missing are query/path/body secrets, alternate serializers, arrays/multiple headers, custom/vendor credential headers, error logs, child loggers, raw headers and property-based leak tests.
units.designRationale: Prevent common browser and API credentials from leaking through automatic HTTP request/response serialization.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted operators need useful request telemetry without exposing Identity, Connector, approval or enterprise-data credentials.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as a last-line regression suite. Company OS should log an allowlisted request envelope rather than full headers/body by default, attach typed sensitivity at ingestion, use deployment-configurable secret-header registration and run leak-canary tests across every log/export sink.
units.responsibilityConflict: A fixed path list cannot prove that evidence/log exports are safe; new Connector headers or credentials in URLs and bodies bypass it. Redacted operational logs also cannot replace immutable source evidence and transform records.
evidence: 15683000 fix: redact HTTP cookies from server logs (#7977)

units.function: Unit tests parsing an environment-configured Express trust-proxy policy into unset, trust-all, hop-count, named subnet or CIDR-list forms while rejecting malformed tokens.
units.dependencyDirection: An ambient deployment environment string enters a strict parser and is assigned directly to Express's trust proxy setting, which controls client IP/protocol/host interpretation downstream.
units.keyDataModels: Undefined/false/0, boolean true, positive hop count, loopback/uniquelocal named ranges, IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs and invalid token errors.
units.lifecycle: Startup leaves Express's safe default unchanged for unset-like values, accepts explicit trusted forms with trimming, and throws on leading-zero integers, internal whitespace or unknown/partially invalid tokens.
units.testAssessment: The parser matrix is detailed and fail-closed for malformed input. Missing are negative/zero/overflow hop values, duplicate/overlapping ranges, IPv4-mapped IPv6, link-local/private named sets, actual spoofed X-Forwarded-* integration behavior, variable proxy-chain lengths, deployment-profile defaults and stable startup diagnostic codes.
units.designRationale: Support reverse-proxy deployments without silently accepting malformed trust configuration or enabling proxy trust by default.
units.companyOsProblem: Identity, tenant routing, rate limiting and audit attribution depend on trustworthy network origin across managed cloud, on-prem ingress and hybrid Connector nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit parser and safe unset default, but reject trust-all in production profiles and avoid hop counts where route length can vary. Require profile-owned CIDR/named-network policy, startup validation and integration tests proving spoofed forwarded headers remain untrusted outside the declared ingress path.
units.responsibilityConflict: A misconfigured trust-all or hop-count policy lets an external caller forge origin metadata used by security and audit decisions. Network origin is context only and must never establish accountable-human identity or approval authority.
evidence: 937fe62d feat(server): TRUST_PROXY supports CIDR list + named subnets (supersedes #3729) (#5872)

units.function: Logger configuration regression test requiring pino-pretty targets to render human-readable timestamps in the process-local timezone using SYS:HH:MM:ss.
units.dependencyDirection: Logger module initialization builds mocked Pino transports; console/file pretty-printer options consume process timezone only at presentation time.
units.keyDataModels: Pino transport target options, translateTime format string, epoch milliseconds and UTC versus Asia/Singapore display values.
units.lifecycle: Importing the logger must configure each pretty target with SYS:HH:MM:ss; a separate Intl check shows one epoch renders differently in UTC and UTC+8.
units.testAssessment: The first test locks the actual logger option. The second does not exercise pino-pretty or mutate process TZ despite its comment; it only proves Intl timezone formatting, so it is indirect evidence for the library contract. Missing are structured UTC timestamps, DST/invalid TZ behavior, multiple transports, production JSON logs, locale independence and correlation with database/event times.
units.designRationale: Make local operator console timestamps match the machine's expected wall clock instead of always appearing as UTC.
units.companyOsProblem: Operators in China and global deployments need localized display, while responsibility evidence requires one canonical, comparable temporal ordering.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY for console presentation. Company OS events and evidence must store UTC instants plus source clock/offset and ordering metadata; Web/CLI localize at the edge. Add a real formatter integration test if this display behavior is retained.
units.responsibilityConflict: A timezone-only HH:MM:ss string is ambiguous across dates, DST and nodes and cannot support responsibility ordering or nonrepudiation. It must never be the canonical audit timestamp.
